questions.q: The total cost of 5 pens and 3 notebooks is 130. If the cost of pen is decreased by 25% and that of the notebook is increased by 10% then total cost of 3 pens and 2 notebooks will be 67. what is the total original cost (in Rs) of 6 pens and 4 notebook?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, linear equations wale sawaalo me decimals aur fractions sabse bade dushman hote hain. Inko sabse pehle gayab kiya kar ke exact whole numbers banaya kar.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Equation set kar, multiplier laga kar decimals hata, aur ek variable udakar answer nikal de!

Mathematically :-
$$5P + 3N = 130$$
$$3(0.75P) + 2(1.1N) = 67 \implies 2.25P + 2.2N = 67$$
$$\text{Multiply by 20 } \implies 45P + 44N = 1340$$
$$\text{Multiply Eq1 by 9 } \implies 45P + 27N = 1170$$
$$17N = 170 \implies N = 10 \implies 5P = 130 - 30 \implies P = 20$$
$$6P + 4N = 6(20) + 4(10) = 120 + 40 = 160$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Variables leke normal elimination kar, bas decimal me fasne se bacha lena khud ko.

Mathematically :-
$$2.25P + 2.2N = 67 \times 100 = 225P + 220N = 6700$$

Exam Takeaway: Decimal equations dikhte hi unhe turant 10, 20 ya 100 se multiply karke whole numbers me le aaya kar, aadhi calculation mistakes wahi khatam ho jayengi.

List IList II
Avoid float mathMultiply equation to remove decimals

questions.q: An ore contains 25% of an alloy that has 90% iron. Other than this, in the remaining 75% of the ore, there is no iron. How many kilograms of the ore are needed to obtain 60 kg of pure iron?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 1. CPR (Constant Product Ratio)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, poore ore me loha kahan se aa raha hai? Sirf uss $25\%$ wale hisse se. Aur usme bhi pura loha nahi hai, bas uska $90\%$ hai. Toh seedha net percentage nikal le iron ka.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Overall iron ka percentage nikal aur seedha usko $60$ ke barabar rakh de!

Mathematically :-
$$\text{Net Iron} = 25\% \times 90\% = 22.5\%$$
$$X \times 22.5\% = 60$$
$$X = \frac{60}{0.225} = \frac{60,000}{225} = 266.67$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Maan le Total Ore $100x$ hai aur basic steps follow kar.

Mathematically :-
$$\text{Alloy} = 25x$$
$$\text{Iron} = 90\% \text{ of } 25x = 22.5x$$
$$22.5x = 60 \implies x = \frac{60}{22.5}$$
$$100x = 100 \times \frac{60}{22.5} \approx 266.67$$

Exam Takeaway: Percentage of percentage dikhe toh hamesha unhe multiply karke ek single net percentage bana liya kar, bahut time bachega.

List IList II
Net Iron %$25\% \times 90\% = 22.5\%$

questions.q: Quantity I- A bar is creating a new signature drink. They are using two alcoholic ingredients in the drink: whisky and brandy. They are using two non-alcoholic ingredients in the drink: Apple juice and Grapes juice. The alcoholic ingredients contain 75% alcohol. The non-alcoholic ingredients contain no alcohol. How many liters of non-alcoholic ingredients must be added to 13 liters of alcoholic ingredients to produce a mixture that is 15% alcohol? Quantity II - Out of a total 108 children playing chess or ludo or both, total number of girls in the group is 80% of the total number of boys in the group. The number of boys playing only chess is 40% of the number of boys and the total number of boys playing chess is 60% of the total number of boys. The number of children playing only ludo is 50% of the total number of children and a total of 12 children play chess and ludo both. What is the number of girls playing only chess ?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: JSM/Deviation

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, ye Data Sufficiency/Quantity comparison wala setup hai. I me Alligation dikh raha hai (0, 75, 15). II me Venn aur set theory lag rahi hai. Dono ko freely todna hai, equation me nhi fasna.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Q1 me seedhi alligation ratio aur Q2 me fast mental Venn sets breakdown.

Mathematically :-
$$Q_I: Ratio(Alc : Non) = (15-0) : (75-15) = 15 : 60 = 1 : 4 \\\\ Alc(1 \ unit) = 13 \Rightarrow Non(4 \ units) = 52 \\\\ Q_{II}: Girls = \frac{4}{5} Boys \Rightarrow 9x = 108 \Rightarrow G=48, B=60 \\\\ Only \ Ludo(Total) = 54 \\\\ Only \ Ludo(B) = 60 - 24(Only \ Chess) - 12(Both) = 24 \\\\ Only \ Ludo(G) = 54 - 24 = 30 \\\\ Only \ Chess(G) = Total \ G(48) - Only \ Ludo(G)(30) - Both(G)(0) = 18 \\\\ 52 > 18 \Rightarrow Q_I > Q_{II}$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Equations likh kar solve karo aur dono parameters derive karo.

Mathematically :-
$$Q_I: 0.75 \times 13 = 0.15 \times (13 + x) \Rightarrow 9.75 = 1.95 + 0.15x \Rightarrow x = 52 \\\\ Q_{II}: n(G)=48, n(B)=60, n(C \cap L)=12, n(Only L)=54 \\\\ n(C_B)=36 \Rightarrow n(Both_B)=36-24=12 \Rightarrow n(Both_G)=0 \\\\ n(OnlyC_G) = n(G) - n(OnlyL_G) - n(Both_G) = 48 - (54 - 24) - 0 = 18 \\\\ Q_I > Q_{II}$$

Exam Takeaway: Data comparison type questions me dono statements rapidly alag-alag framework me break down karne padte hain.

questions.q: B's required target was $20\%$ more than A's. However, A completed his target but B completed only $80\%$ of his target. If B completed 96 units, what was A's target?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, bina pen uthaye options se game khel! B ne 96 complete kiye, jo uske original (badhe hue) target ka 80% hai. Toh A ka target 100 ke aas-paas hi hoga.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Maan le A ka target $100$ unit hai. Jab tumhara assumed ratio aur question ki exact value match ho jaye toh A ka assumed target $100$ units hi absolute correct hai. Exam me wahi ruk ja aur tick maar!

Mathematically :-
$$ A_{target} = 100 \\\\ B_{target} = 120 \\\\ B_{done} = 120 \\times \\frac{80}{100} = 96 \\\\ 96 \\ units = 96 \\\\ 100 \\ units = 100 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Algebra use karle agar dar lagta hai. Same baat hui na!

Mathematically :-
$$ Let \\ A = x \\\\ B = 1.2x \\\\ B_{done} = 0.8 \\times 1.2x = 0.96x \\\\ 0.96x = 96 \\\\ x = 100 $$

Exam Takeaway: Hamesha percentage scaling ko $100$ base se start kar, max time exact value direct match ho jati hai SSC exams me.

questions.q: Vikas has Rs.x. He gave 44.44% of Rs.x to Anju. Anju bought 33.33% of the money she got from Vikas for a dress and donated 31.25% of the remaining amount. The remaining amount is saved by (y). If the amount donated is 1250, then find the value of (x-y).
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 2. Successive Change (The Chain Reaction)

Pen-Free Observation: Ye pure fraction chain ka chakkar hai. $44.44\% = \frac{4}{9}$, $33.33\% = \frac{1}{3}$, aur $31.25\% = \frac{5}{16}$. Branches ko pakad ke bas link karta ja!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai, sequence utha le: Anju ko mila $\frac{4}{9}x$.
Dress pe uda diye $\frac{1}{3}$, bache hue $\frac{2}{3}$.
Toh Remaining amount aaya $= \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{4}{9}x = \frac{8}{27}x$.
Donation hua $31.25\%$ yani remaining ka $\frac{5}{16}$ part.
Donation $= \frac{5}{16} \times \frac{8}{27}x = \frac{5}{54}x$. Aur yehi 1250 hai.
$\frac{5}{54}x = 1250 \implies x = 13500$.
Ab Save $(y)$ hua bacha hua $\frac{11}{16}$ hissa.
$y = \frac{11}{16} \times \frac{8}{27}x = \frac{11}{54}x$.
Value rakh $y = \frac{11}{54} \times 13500 = 2750$.
Pucha kya hai? $x - y = 13500 - 2750 = 10750$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Ek bade percentage wale lambaue sawal ko tu single equation ratios me baant sakta hai jo tezi se cancel ho jaati hai.

Exam Takeaway: Ajeeb fractions jaise $31.25\% = 5 \times 6.25\% = \frac{5}{16}$ rate hue hone chahiye warna waqt bekar kharab hoga.

Percentage TableFraction Form
44.44%, 31.25%4/9, 5/16

questions.q: The price of an article increased by $16.66\%$ every year. If the difference between the price at the end of third and fourth year is 126 then 1/8th of the price at the end of second year?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 2. Successive Change (The Chain Reaction)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, $16.66\%$ badhne ka fraction 1/6 hota hai. Koi chiz 3rd year se 4th year me jayegi, toh kitna badhegi? Apne aap ka 1/6 hi badhegi na! Yahi trick thi isme.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): 4th year aur 3rd year ka difference, purely 3rd year ki value ka $1/6$ hai. Toh $3\text{rd yr} \times 1/6 = 126 \implies 3\text{rd yr} = 756$. Ab isse backward ja 2nd year pe (multiply by 6/7). $756 \times 6/7 = 648$. Iska $1/8$ nikal, $648 / 8 = 81$. Ratio method is supreme!

Mathematically :-
$\text{Diff} = P_3 \times \frac{1}{6} = 126$
$P_3 = 756$
$P_2 = 756 \times \frac{6}{7} = 648$
$\text{Ans} = \frac{648}{8} = 81$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): $P \times (7/6)^3$ aur $P \times (7/6)^4$ leke dono ko minus karke P ki value nikalne jayega toh adha exam wahi khatam ho jayega.

Mathematically :-
$P(1+\frac{1}{6})^4 - P(1+\frac{1}{6})^3 = 126$
$P(\frac{7}{6})^3 (\frac{7}{6} - 1) = 126$
$P_3 \times \frac{1}{6} = 126 \implies P_3 = 756$
$P_2 \times \frac{7}{6} = 756 \implies P_2 = 648$
$\frac{P_2}{8} = 81$

Exam Takeaway: Compound growth me adjacent years ka difference direct fraction increase ki value bata deta hai.

StepMultiplier
Backward Shift$\times 6/7$

questions.q: A milkman bought 50 litres of milk for Rs. 2000. 5 litres spoiled. At what rate per litre should he sell the remaining milk to make a profit of 20% on his total outlay?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, milkman ko sirf apne kharche pe overall $20\%$ profit chahiye. Usko is baat se koi matlab nahi ki kitna doodh kharab hua hai, usko bas aakhiri revenue nikalna hai bache hue doodh se.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Total revenue target set kar aur bachi hui quantity se divide maar de, answer teri aankhon ke samne hoga!

Mathematically :-
$$\text{Target Revenue} = 2000 \times 1.2 = 2400$$
$$\text{Remaining Qty} = 50 - 5 = 45$$
$$\text{Selling Rate} = \frac{2400}{45} = 53.33$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Per unit cost wagera nikal ke bewakoofo ki tarah solution complicate mat karna.

Mathematically :-
$$\text{CP per L} = 40 \implies \text{Logic fails here without total target}$$

Exam Takeaway: Seedha target total revenue nikal aur remaining quantity se divide kar de. Profit/Loss me quantities destroy hone wale questions ka ye best hack hai!

questions.q: Every month, a man consumes 15 kg of rice and 6 kg of wheat. The price of rice is $20\%$ of the price of wheat, resulting in a total expenditure of 225 per month for rice and wheat combined. If the price of wheat is increased by $12\%$, what percentage reduction in rice consumption is needed to maintain the same expenditure of 225? (Given that price of rice and consumption of wheat is constant)
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: CPR (Constant Product Ratio) / Unitary Scaling Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, price of Rice $20\%$ of Wheat hai, yani inka price ratio 1:5 hoga. Kharcha maintain karna hai toh idhar ka paisa udhar compensate karna padega. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): R:W price ratio 1:5 hai. Maan le Rice Rs. $x$/kg, Wheat Rs. $5x$/kg. Total bill: $15(x) + 6(5x) = 45x$. Par total kharcha 225 diya hai $\implies 45x = 225 \implies x = 5$. Toh Rice = Rs. 5/kg, Wheat = Rs. 25/kg. Ab Wheat price 12% bada, yani $25 \times 0.12 = 3$ Rs badha per kg. 6 kg wheat pe Rs. 18 ka extra phatka. Total bill 225 hi rakhna hai toh ye 18 Rs Rice kam khakar bachana hoga. 1 kg Rice 5 ka hai. Kitna Rice kam aayega? $\frac{18}{5} = 3.6$ kg. Pehle rice khata tha 15 kg. Percentage reduction = $\frac{3.6}{15} \times 100 = 24\%$. Method 2 (Concept Builder): Ek ek value ko fraction me handle kar, par equations lamba padenge. Focus on 'extra cost' compensation. Exam Takeaway: Expense maintaining wale sawalo me pura recalculate mat kar. Sirf "Extra Badha Hua Kharcha = Doosri taraf bachi hui unit" pe equate kar.

questions.q: A company allowed $16\%$ commission on the total sales made by salesman and a bonus of $6\%$ on the sales over 7000. If the salesman deposited $\text{Rs. } 8610$ in the company after deducting his earning from the total sales made by him. Find total sales?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: JSM/Deviation.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, imaginary commission method se salesman ko starting ke 7000 par bhi $6\%$ bonus de de, toh overall uniform $22\%$ commission ban jayega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Shift method. Mathematically :-
$$Extra\_Bonus = 6\% \text{ of } 7000 = 420$$
$$New\_Deposit = 8610 - 420 = 8190$$
$$78\% = 8190$$
$$100\% = 10500$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Basic algebra. Mathematically :-
$$S = \text{Total Sales}$$
$$S - [0.16S + 0.06(S - 7000)] = 8610$$
$$S - 0.22S + 420 = 8610$$
$$0.78S = 8190 \Rightarrow S = 10500$$

Exam Takeaway: Imaginary len-den se rate uniform banaya kar, bahut time bachega aur calculations seedhi 1 step me aayengi.

List IList II
Income ShiftingHypothetically uniform the commission to find the base easily.

questions.q: A mixture contains $60\%$ milk. If 20 liters of water is added to the 80-liter mixture, what is the new percentage of milk? (CGL TIER I - $\frac{22}{09}$/2025 - SHIFT 3)
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, mixture me paani daloge toh paani badlega, lekin milk ki absolute amount constant rahegi. Wahi nikal ke naye base par percentage bana de.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Constant element tracking. Mathematically :-
$$Milk = 80 \times 0.60 = 48$$
$$New\_Total = 80 + 20 = 100$$
$$\% = \frac{48}{100} \times 100 = 48\%$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Fractional proportion. Mathematically :-
$$Milk = \frac{3}{5} \times 80 = 48$$
$$Water = \frac{2}{5} \times 80 = 32$$
$$New\_Water = 32 + 20 = 52$$
$$\% = \frac{48}{48+52} \times 100 = 48\%$$

Exam Takeaway: Mixture me jo element intact rahe usi absolute value ko total target par naya percentage banane ke liye use kar.

List IList II
Constant AnchorNever track the changing element, track what remains unchanged.

questions.q: A fraction $\frac{3}{5}$ is decreased by $\frac{2}{5}$. The resulting fraction is then increased by 20%.\n\nWhat is the percentage decrease/increase in the value of the original fraction?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, base me 5 hai dono jagah. $ rac{3}{5}$ me se $ rac{2}{5}$ gaya toh bacha $ rac{1}{5}$. Ab $ rac{1}{5}$ ko 20% (yani khud ka $ rac{1}{5}$th) badhana hai. Seedha seedha base ko 25 dimaag me soch aur numerators ko 15 aur 6 padh. 15 se 6 hua, matlab 9 ka loss 15 par. $ rac{9}{15}$ seedha 60% hota hai! Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Base same kar lo taaki fractions integers jaise behave karein. Mathematically :-
$ ext{Original} = rac{3}{5} = rac{15}{25}$
$ ext{New} = ( rac{3}{5} - rac{2}{5}) imes 1.2 = rac{1}{5} imes rac{6}{5} = rac{6}{25}$
$\% ext{ Decrease} = rac{15 - 6}{15} imes 100 = 60\%$ Method 2 (Concept Builder): Basic se chalte hain. Pehle original fraction me se fraction minus karo, fir jo aaye usko 20% increase karo (multiply by $ rac{6}{5}$). Mathematically :-
$ ext{Original} = rac{3}{5}$
$ ext{After subtraction} = rac{3}{5} - rac{2}{5} = rac{1}{5}$
$ ext{After 20\% increase} = rac{1}{5} imes (1 + rac{20}{100}) = rac{1}{5} imes rac{6}{5} = rac{6}{25}$
$ ext{Absolute Change} = rac{3}{5} - rac{6}{25} = rac{15}{25} - rac{6}{25} = rac{9}{25}$
$ ext{Percentage Change} = rac{ rac{9}{25}}{ rac{15}{25}} imes 100 = rac{9}{15} imes 100 = 60\%$ Exam Takeaway: Is type ke questions me "decreased by a fraction" aur "decreased by a percentage" ka phrasing hi trap hota hai. Hamesha final aur initial fraction ka base same kar lo (jaise yahan humne dono ko 25 bana liya), toh calculation seconds me muh-zabani ho jayegi.
List IList II
Base EqualizationWhenever comparing fractions to find percentage change, equalize their denominators.
Fractional MultiplierFor a 20% increase, directly multiply by $ rac{6}{5}$ instead of calculating 20% and adding it back.

questions.q: A fraction in reduced form is such that when it is squared and then its numerator is increased by $25\%$ and the denominator is reduced to $80\%$ it results in $\frac{5}{8}$ of the original fraction. The product of the numerator and denominator is:
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, fraction par percentage operations sidha unke multipliers se likhe jaane chahiye. Increase $25\%$ means $5/4$, and reduced to $80\%$ means $4/5$. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Maan le original fraction $\frac{N}{D}$ hai. Isko square kiya toh bana $\frac{N^2}{D^2}$. Numerator ko $25\%$ badhaya yani $\frac{5}{4}$ kiya. Denominator ko $80\%$ kar diya yani $\frac{4}{5}$ kiya. Naya fraction bana: $\frac{(\frac{5}{4}) N^2}{(\frac{4}{5}) D^2} = \frac{25}{16} \frac{N^2}{D^2}$. Question kehta hai ki ye value original fraction ka $\frac{5}{8}$ hai. Toh equate kar de: $\frac{25}{16} \frac{N^2}{D^2} = \frac{5}{8} \frac{N}{D}$. Ek $\frac{N}{D}$ cancel ho gaya. Bacha $\frac{N}{D} = \frac{5}{8} \times \frac{16}{25} = \frac{2}{5}$. Toh apna original fraction $\frac{2}{5}$ tha. Numerator $\times$ Denominator = $2 \times 5 = 10$. Method 2 (Concept Builder): Variables le kar lamba karega toh equation ulajh jayegi. Cancel out as soon as possible. Exam Takeaway: "Reduced TO" aur "Reduced BY" ka language dhyan se padha kar. Yahan reduced TO $80\%$ tha, yani direct $4/5$ lagana hai.
OperationMultiplier
Numerator $+25\%$$5/4$
Denominator to $80\%$$4/5$

questions.q: In a village, two contestants (A & B) are contesting in an election. 70% of the registered voters cast their votes in the election and A wins the election by 400 votes. If A had received 12.5% less votes, A’s votes would have been equal to B’s votes. How many registered voters are there in the village?
questions.s:
Tool Triggered: 5. Unitary Scaling

The "Pen-Free" Observation First:
Dekh bhai, $12.5\%$ ka fraction $1/8$ hai. A ne apne 1/8 hissa lose kiya, wahi hissa B ke paas chala gaya. Toh A aur B ka equality equation banta hai: $A - A/8 = B + A/8$. Seedha B = $3A/4$. Ratio $A:B$ = 4:3. Margin 1 unit ka 400. Total cast 7 unit = 2800. Ye total ka $70\%$ hai. Toh 100% = 4000.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Value transfer logic.

Mathematically :-
$$ A - \frac{1}{8}A = B + \frac{1}{8}A \\ \frac{7}{8}A = B + \frac{1}{8}A \implies B = \frac{6}{8}A = \frac{3}{4}A \\ \frac{A}{B} = \frac{4}{3} \\ \text{Margin} = 4 - 3 = 1 \text{ unit} \\ 1 \text{ unit} = 400 \implies \text{Casted} (7 \text{ units}) = 2800 \\ 70\% \text{ of Reg} = 2800 \implies \text{Reg} = \frac{2800}{0.7} = 4000 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Standard percentage equation.

Mathematically :-
$$ \text{Condition: } A - 12.5\% A = B + 12.5\% A \\ 87.5\% A = B + 12.5\% A \implies B = 75\% A \\ \text{Diff} = A - B = A - 0.75A = 0.25A \\ 0.25 A = 400 \implies A = 1600 \\ B = 0.75 \times 1600 = 1200 \\ \text{Total Cast} = A + B = 1600 + 1200 = 2800 \\ \text{Reg} = \frac{2800 \times 100}{70} = 4000 $$

Exam Takeaway: Election questions me vote transfer ki theory directly fractions par execute karo.

questions.q: Due to an increase of $32\%$ in the price of pulse, a person reduces his consumption in such a way that his expenditure increases only by $10\%$. If he consumes 150 kg of pulse after the price has increased, then how much pulse was consumed by him initially?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: CPR.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, Constant Product Ratio (CPR) ki ninja trick laga, Initial aur Final consumption ka seedha fraction nikal.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): CPR direct fraction. Mathematically :-
$$\frac{Initial}{Final} = \frac{100 + P\%}{100 + E\%} = \frac{132}{110} = \frac{6}{5}$$
$$5 \rightarrow 150 \Rightarrow 1 \rightarrow 30$$
$$6 \rightarrow 180$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Traditional formula. Mathematically :-
$$P_{new} = 1.32 P_{old}$$
$$E_{new} = 1.10 E_{old}$$
$$C_{new} = \frac{E_{new}}{P_{new}} = \frac{1.10}{1.32} C_{old} = \frac{5}{6} C_{old}$$
$$\frac{5}{6} C_{old} = 150 \Rightarrow C_{old} = 180$$

Exam Takeaway: Price aur Expenditure ke percentages diye hon toh formula me base swap karke consumption ka ratio instantly ban jata hai.

List IList II
Ratio Direct HackC1 / C2 = (100 + E2\%) / (100 + P2\%) doesn't hold. Right hack is Initial/Final = (100+New Price) / (100+New Exp).

questions.q: 10,000 voters vote to elect their mayor. A receives 500 votes more than that of B and wins the election. $5\%$ of the votes are invalid. If a news TV channel predicts that after 5 years the number of voters will increase by $50\%$ and A will receive $10\%$ votes less than that he received now, how many votes will B get at that time? (Assume all the votes as valid after 5 years and only A and B stand in the election in both the time)
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling / JSM Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, linear calculations hain. Total vote aur winning margin diya ho toh dono candidates ke vote verbally add/subtract karke nikalne aane chahiye. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Pehle present data nikal. 10,000 ka $5\%$ (500) invalid ho gaye. Valid bache $9500$. Ab A aur B me equation banegi: $A + B = 9500$ aur margin $A - B = 500$. Dono equations ko add karega toh $2A = 10000 \implies A = 5000$. Matlab B ko abhi $4500$ mile hain. TV prediction pe aa: 5 saal baad total voters $50\%$ badh jayenge (sab valid) = $15000$. A ko pichle bar se $10\%$ kam vote milenge, yani $5000$ ka $90\% = 4500$. B ke vote nikalne ke liye bache hue vote pakad: $15000 - 4500 = 10500$ vote! Method 2 (Concept Builder): Ek ek ko variables me assume karega toh confuse ho jayega. Values round hain toh sidha data pe khel. Exam Takeaway: Sum and Difference equations ($x+y=A, x-y=B$) ko mentally solve karna seekho.

questions.q: A contractor estimated that a project would cost $\text{Rs. }     5$,00,000. He planned for $60\%$ of the cost to go to materials, $25\%$ to labor, and the rest as contingency. However, due to delays, material cost increased by $12.5\%$, labor cost increased by $10\%$, and contingency remained unchanged. What is the new total cost? (CHSL TIER I - $\frac{30}{11}$/2025 - SHIFT 1)
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: JSM / Deviation

Pen-Free Observation: Original 5 Lakh ko tod mat, seedha un percentages ka deviation effect nikal ke jod de.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Material $60\%$ pe $12.5\%$ change $= 7.5\%$ effect. Labour $25\%$ pe $10\%$ change $= 2.5\%$ effect. Net change $= +10\%$. 5 Lakh ka $10\%$ ($50,000$) badha de $= 5,50,000$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Har part ko rupees me calculate kar: Material 3L, Labor 1.25L. Phir unpe individually percent badha ke jodd. Bahut lamba calculation padega.

Exam Takeaway: Over-all change sum of base deviations se jaldi nikalta hai, absolute figures end me dekhi jati hain.

questions.q: In order to maximise his gain, a theatre owner decides to reduce the price of tickets by $15\%$ and as a result of this the sales of tickets increases by $35\%$. If as a result of this, the sales of tickets increases his weekly collection by 25200. Then find by what value did the gross collection increase per day?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change (The Chain Reaction) - TRICK IDENTIFICATION

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, examiner maje le raha hai. Start percentages se kara par ant me sidha rupay me value de di. Toh hum kyu formula lagayen? Divisibility by $7$ ka khel hai bas.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Ye question pura scam hai! Pucha hai 'increase per day'! Toh bhai mere, seedha $1$ hafte ke collection ko $7$ se divide karna tha! Aankhein khuli rakh paper me! Mathematically :- $$ \text{Increase per day} = \frac{\text{Weekly Increase}}{7} \\ \text{Increase} = \frac{25200}{7} = 3600 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Agar tum concept pe gaye toh net effect nikaloge, fir equation solve karoge. Itna bada trap bicha rakha hai wahan mat fans jana. Mathematically :- $$ \text{Net } \% = -15 + 35 - \frac{15 \times 35}{100} = +14.75\% \\ 14.75\% \text{ of Total} = 25200 \text{ (Useless calc)} \\ \text{Per day} = \frac{25200}{7} = 3600 $$

Exam Takeaway: Arithmetic data dekh kar blind formula mat lagaya karo. Last line ki demand check karna sabse bada weapon hai.

TrapReality

questions.q:
A farm cultivates Maize and Soybeans. The ratio of the land area allocated to Maize and Soybeans is 3:2. Initially, both crops yield the exact same amount of produce per acre.

This year, the land area for Maize was increased by 25% but its yield per acre dropped by 4%. Meanwhile, the area for Soybeans was increased by 40% but its yield per acre plummeted by 30%. What is the overall percentage change in the total farm production?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change + Weighted Average (JSM) Pen-Free Observation: Yahan koi total fix nahi hai, sab kuch badal raha hai aur final overall change pucha hai. Pehle dono fasalon ka alag-alag net successive nikal. Maize ka area badha aur yield ghata ($+25, -4$), iska successive aayega $+20\%$. Soybeans ka ($+40, -30$), successive aaya $-2\%$. Ab in dono percentages ko inke initial production base ratio ($3:2$) par JSM se mila de. Total deviation nikal aur total base se divide maar! Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Successive nikal kar direct JSM (Weighted Average) laga. Mathematically :-
$\text{Production Ratio (Maize : Soy)} = (3 \times 1) : (2 \times 1) = 3 : 2$
$\text{Maize Net Change} = 25 - 4 - \frac{25 \times 4}{100} = +20\%$
$\text{Soybeans Net Change} = 40 - 30 - \frac{40 \times 30}{100} = -2\%$
$\text{Net Deviation} = (3 \times 20) + (2 \times -2) = 60 - 4 = +56$
$\text{Overall \% Change} = \frac{+56}{3 + 2} = \frac{56}{5} = +11.2\%$ Method 2 (Concept Builder): Absolute data assume karke final total nikalna. Mathematically :-
$\text{Let Area (Maize = 300, Soy = 200) and Yield = 10 units/acre}$
$\text{Initial Prod} = (300 \times 10) + (200 \times 10) = 3000 + 2000 = 5000$
$\text{New Maize Prod} = (300 \times 1.25) \times (10 \times 0.96) = 375 \times 9.6 = 3600$
$\text{New Soy Prod} = (200 \times 1.40) \times (10 \times 0.70) = 280 \times 7 = 1960$
$\text{Total New Prod} = 3600 + 1960 = 5560$
$\% \text{ Change} = \frac{5560 - 5000}{5000} \times 100 = 11.2\%$ Exam Takeaway: Successive aur JSM SSC/CDS ke sabse powerful core tools hain. Jab variables multiple dimensions me change hon, toh hamesha unhe Successive se ek single 1D percentage me sikod lo, aur uske baad normal JSM/Average laga lo.
Data ComponentTool Applied
Individual Crop ($Area \times Yield$)Successive Change
Overall Farm ($Crop_1 + Crop_2$)JSM / Weighted Average

questions.q: Rahul manages an E-sports team with 3 distinct players: X, Y, and Z. In every multiplayer match, the rules dictate that he must field exactly 2 players from his team. Based on the tournament's reward system: If X wins a match, Rahul's team wallet increases by 15% of the balance he had before the match. If Y wins, it increases by 25%. If Z wins, it increases by 10%. However, if any of his fielded players loses, his wallet decreases by 5% of the balance he had before the match. Yesterday, the team played 4 consecutive matches. Y won Match 1 and Match 3. X won Match 2, and Z won Match 4. If Rahul's final wallet balance exactly at the end of the day was Rs. 16,632, in which specific match did Rahul's wallet gain the maximum absolute amount of money?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 2. Successive Change (The Chain Reaction)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, jab percentages lagatar same base par badh aur ghat rahi hain match-by-match, to seedha successive multiplication ka game hai. Matlab har match ki starting base value par (Win \% - 5\%) ka net impact aayega!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dimaag me net percentage nikalo har match ka. Max percentage increase Match 1 aur 3 me hai ($20\%$). Lekin Match 3 ka base Match 1 se bada hoga. 10 second me answer.

Mathematically :-
$$ M1: +25\\% - 5\\% = +20\\% \\ (1.2x) \\\\ M2: +15\\% - 5\\% = +10\\% \\ (1.1x) \\\\ M3: +25\\% - 5\\% = +20\\% \\ (1.2x) \\\\ M4: +10\\% - 5\\% = +5\\% \\ (1.05x) \\\\ Total = 1.2 \\times 1.1 \\times 1.2 \\times 1.05 = 1.6632 \\\\ Initial = \\frac{16632}{1.6632} = 10000 \\\\ M3 \\ Base > M1 \\ Base \\implies M3 \\ max $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Proper initial start base lo aur har match ki calculations dikha kar check karo.

Mathematically :-
$$ Start = 10000 \\\\ M1 \\ Gain = 10000 \\times 0.20 = 2000 \\\\ M2 \\ Gain = 12000 \\times 0.10 = 1200 \\\\ M3 \\ Gain = 13200 \\times 0.20 = 2640 \\\\ M4 \\ Gain = 15840 \\times 0.05 = 792 $$

Exam Takeaway: Hamesha dhyan rakhna, jab successive increase ho raha ho, to highest percentage on the highest base will always yield the maximum absolute value.

questions.q: At the beginning of day 1 of a month, Rajesh has 500 eggs. He sells 20% of the eggs by the end of the day and added b% of the eggs at the beginning of the next day and sold 20% of the eggs at the end of the next day. This pattern continued up to the end of the third day of the month when he is left with 1024 eggs. The value of b is equal to:
questions.s:
Tool Triggered: 2. Successive Change

The "Pen-Free" Observation First:
Dekh bhai, sequence break kar. Day 1 ke end me 500 ka $80\%$ bacha (yani 400). Fir 2 din same multiplier laga. 400 se badhkar 1024 pahuchna hai. Perfect square banega. Option se utha, agar $b=100$ (yani double), toh $400 \times 2 = 800$, usme se $20\%$ gaye bache 640. Phir agle din $640 \times 2 = 1280$, $20\%$ gaye bache 1024. Match ho gaya!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Hit and Trial sequence.

Mathematically :-
$$ \text{End of Day 1} = 500 \times 0.8 = 400 \\ \text{Check } b=100 \implies \text{add } 100\% \implies \text{multiply by } 2 \\ \text{End of Day 2} = (400 \times 2) \times 0.8 = 800 \times 0.8 = 640 \\ \text{End of Day 3} = (640 \times 2) \times 0.8 = 1280 \times 0.8 = 1024 \text{ (Matched!)} $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Full equation with successive multipliers.

Mathematically :-
$$ 400 \times \left(1 + \frac{b}{100}\right)^2 \times (0.8)^2 = 1024 \\ 400 \times \left(1 + \frac{b}{100}\right)^2 \times 0.64 = 1024 \\ 256 \times \left(1 + \frac{b}{100}\right)^2 = 1024 \\ \left(1 + \frac{b}{100}\right)^2 = \frac{1024}{256} = 4 \\ 1 + \frac{b}{100} = 2 \implies \frac{b}{100} = 1 \implies b = 100 $$

Exam Takeaway: Complex equation me hamesha perfect square pattern dhundha kar aur option satisfy karaya kar.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Pehle net percentage nikal le: $20 + 12 + 2.4 = 34.4\%$. 200 ka $34.4\%$ hota hai $68.8$. Add kiya toh $268.8$.

Exam Takeaway: Jab initial value given ho aur rate easy fractions me na ho, toh decimal multiplier lagana best hota hai.

questions.q: If first number is $8\frac{1}{3}\%$ less than third number and ratio of second and third number is 15:16 then average of first and third number is how much percent less/more than second number?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, $8\frac{1}{3}\%$ hota hai $1/12$. Matlab 1st aur 3rd ka ratio 11:12 hai. Udhar 2nd aur 3rd ka 15:16 hai. Third number ko equal kar, sab sort ho jayega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): 12 aur 16 ka LCM 48 hota hai. 3rd ko 48 banayega toh 1st = 44, 2nd = 45 aayega. 1st aur 3rd ka average = 46. 46, 45 se 1 zyada hai 45 pe. $1/45$ seedha $2.22\%$ deta hai.

Mathematically :-
$I:III = 11:12 = 44:48$
$II:III = 15:16 = 45:48$
$\text{Avg}(I, III) = 46$
$\text{Diff} = 46 - 45 = 1$
$\% = \frac{1}{45} \times 100 = 2.22\%$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Ratio balancing aani chahiye. $A:C = 11:12$ aur $B:C = 15:16$. C common hai, toh usey same bana. Fir simply percentage change nikal de naye base B par.

Mathematically :-
$C = 48$
$A = 44$
$B = 45$
$\frac{44+48}{2} = 46$
$\frac{46-45}{45} \times 100 = 2.22\%$

Exam Takeaway: Ratio ko merge karne ke liye humesha LCM ka base shift method use kiya kar, x maan ke mat beth jana!

RatiosScaled

II : III = 15 : 16$45 : 48$

questions.q: The population of a village increases by 8% annually. If the current population is 58,320, what was it two years ago (approx)? (CGL TIER I - 21/09/2025 - SHIFT 2)
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, $8\%$ yani $2/25$. Fraction se ratio square bana. $729$ units ki value $58320$. Dimaag laga, unit digit $9$ me kya multiply kare ki $2$ aaye? $8$ se! Toh multiplier $80$ pakka hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Square ratio bana kar exact multiplier nikal.

Mathematically :-
$$Ratio = (25)^2 : (27)^2 = 625 : 729 \\\\ 729 \ units = 58320 \\\\ 1 \ unit = \frac{58320}{729} = 80 \\\\ Initial = 625 \times 80 = 50000$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Pure amount ka formula lagakar decimals me kaato.

Mathematically :-
$$P(1 + \frac{8}{100})^2 = 58320 \\\\ P(\frac{27}{25})^2 = 58320 \\\\ P \times \frac{729}{625} = 58320 \\\\ P = \frac{58320 \times 625}{729} = 50000$$

Exam Takeaway: Divisibility rules aur unit digit multiplier tracking se calculations kafi time bacha leti hain.

List IList II

questions.q: If 65% of 350 - ?% of 250 + 40% of 120 = 158, then find the value of ?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, equation ko tukdo me tod ke simplify kar. $40\%$ of $120$ toh bacchon wala khel hai, seedha $48$ aayega. $65\%$ of $350$ thoda sa calculative lag raha hai par isko decimal $0.65 \times 350$ likh kar solve kiya ja sakta hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Percentage ko decimal me convert kar aur direct equation solve maar!

Mathematically :-
$$350 \times 0.65 = 227.5$$
$$48 - 2.5x + 227.5 = 158$$
$$275.5 - 2.5x = 158 \implies 2.5x = 117.5$$
$$25x = 1175 \implies x = 47$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Agar calculations me phans raha ho toh Digital Sum (C9) technique se option verify kar liya kar.

Mathematically :-
$$65\% (DS=2) \times 350 (DS=8) \rightarrow 16 \rightarrow 7$$
$$40\% (DS=4) \times 120 (DS=3) \rightarrow 12 \rightarrow 3$$
$$158 \rightarrow DS=5$$
$$7 - 7x + 3 = 5 \implies 10 - 7x = 5 \implies 7x = 5$$
$$7(2) = 14 \rightarrow 5 \implies x=47$$

Exam Takeaway: Digital sum wahan chipkaya kar jahan normal calculation tera extra time kha rahi ho.

questions.q: The number of students in A is (y + 63) which is 47 less than that of B. If the number of boys in B is $\frac{1}{3}$ of the total number of students in B and the number of girls in B is $75\%$ of the total number of students in A, then find the total number of students in B?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling / Cross-Product Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, yahan 'y' wali line ekdum bekaar hai, bas time khane ko di hai. Focus sirf A aur B ke relation aur fractions par rakh. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Pehli line ka saar hai $A = B - 47$. Ab equation banate hain: B me boys $1/3$ hain, toh seedhi baat hai girls $2/3$ hongi. B ki girls $75\%$ (yani $3/4$) of A ke barabar hain. Equation bani: $\frac{2}{3}B = \frac{3}{4}A$. Hamein pata hai $A = B - 47$. Substitute kar de: $\frac{2}{3}B = \frac{3}{4}(B - 47)$. Cross multiply mar de: $8B = 9B - 9 \times 47$. Toh sidha $B = 423$ aayega. Aur yahi pucha hai. Khatam! Method 2 (Concept Builder): Agar fractions uljhane wale lagein toh ratio likh lo. $B_{girls} : B_{total} = 2 : 3$. And $B_{girls} : A_{total} = 3 : 4$. Dono me $B_{girls}$ ko equate karke ratios mila lo. 2 aur 3 ka LCM 6 banao. Toh $B = 9$, $A = 8$. Difference 1 unit = 47. B chahiye toh $9 \times 47 = 423$. Exam Takeaway: Variables dekh kar confuse mat ho. Unhe ratio me ghuma do.
EntityRatio Form
Total B9 units
Total A8 units
